entries.title: Capability guide and automatic coverage checks
entries.where: Repository README → capabilities and user guide; bookmark docs/CAPABILITIES.md.
entries.behavior: Reviewed walkthroughs explain features, exact entry points, limitations and observable tests. The command/gesture inventory regenerates from the application registries. Builds and model checks reject missing command coverage and stale generated guidance. A checked-in pre-push hook, installed per checkout with node --run hooks:install, blocks source pushes unless the working tree is clean at the pushed HEAD and local model tests, preview build and backend type checks pass. Artifact-only GitHack pushes skip duplicate source checks. Failed local checks do not reach GitHub and cannot trigger email. Delivery requires a passing local model/architecture suite before preview pushes, and requested behavior changes update matching assertions. Delivery batches verified source pushes; local frontend success, backend import checks, GitHub CI and browser acceptance are reported separately. Newer PR commits cancel superseded check runs without interrupting master releases.

entries.title: Active context, close, minimize, resize and descendants
entries.where: Master controller → Active context. Click the intended frame first.
entries.behavior: Actions target the clicked/focused frame. Esc steps out one field/popup level before minimizing; active MS has priority. W resizes/restores, M minimizes/restores, X closes, D toggles descendants, subject to saved bindings. Resized windows retain projected bounds and themed borders across focus and minimize/reopen. W restores retained original geometry. Projection styling is independent of React/Rnd wrapper updates. Left-clicking empty space dismisses all open contextual dials and requested dial editors, consuming that press so it does not also draw or begin a world gesture. Dial ×/close buttons are removed; the middle circle remains an unlabelled origin marker at full opacity. Category Back and Escape still step outward. Controls and rendered target roles retain their own click handling. Empty-space dismissal preserves chosen presets and accepted settings. Registered geometry surfaces now supply target adapters to the same commands and shortcuts; frame-only controls remain frame-only. MC discovers contextual controls from the command catalog rather than a parallel geometry toolbar. Delete selection and Compact are projected there. Popup/value-field Escape still precedes geometry scope and its parent frame. Shared active layers expose advance/confirm callbacks. Alt+MB4 steps outward, Alt+MB5 advances the nearest declared stage, Enter confirms, and Escape cancels or steps outward. Plain MB4/5 retain configured history behavior. Omnic dials have no Back/Confirm/checkmark navigation buttons; their centers only drag. Native input Enter remains local.

entries.title: Move, dock, select and organize UI
entries.where: UI library; UI edit mode; shared frame/control context actions.
entries.behavior: Drag actual frame handles or supported control edges. Docking offers destinations when a dragged header reaches another header. UI selection, alignment, compaction and reset are separate from knowledge structure. Window/frame drag previews reuse gesture-local target discovery and read-only docking policy results. Visual movement uses the latest pointer position once per animation frame, with geometry reads before transform writes. Release refreshes destination geometry and commits through the existing shared history; cancellation restores the live payload. Active-context shortcuts defer to a held UI gesture, so Esc cancels the drag before a parent minimize action. Pickup snapshots exclude descendants of the held frame/window and read visibility before lifting, reducing the expand-then-drag setup burst.

entries.title: Horizontal spectrum slider
entries.where: Numeric property editors outside the Composer, including history Steps and visual parameters. Specialized spectrum/dial-size and snap configuration controls retain this path.
entries.behavior: Drag anywhere on the track. Left-click endpoints selects min/max; right-click endpoints edits working limits. Right-click the dot types a value; right-click arrows changes jump size. Working limits cannot override hard renderer/semantic bounds. Manual value, limit and jump editors open as shared child popups at the invoking cursor point. Value/hover updates do not move them. The standalone ½ picker has been removed from the value slider. Prepared rule values use the same slider, with sequence traversal rather than uniform interpolation; minimum/maximum controls remain at its ends. Visible numeric readouts use six significant digits to avoid long floating-point strings crowding nearby controls; exact values remain in tooltips, accessible/native inputs and owner state. The slider declares its whole compound control as a popup boundary, allowing shared child editors to avoid covering its controls. Relative DOF-icon grabs use the shared free-space value scrub: the first three-pixel movement locks a horizontal, vertical or diagonal axis for the drag, further motion projects onto it, and reversing decreases the value.

entries.title: Circular Omnic composer: editing inside, tools on the rim
entries.where: Create → New Omnic object, or select an object → Open Omnic composer. Both open the same circular radar.
entries.behavior: The whole Composer is a circular radar with editing inside and icon tools along its rim. Root tools are hidden by default: hover the shared circular rim axis to reveal them, then move onto a tool. There is no eye/show-hide button. Tools stay revealed while a child category or requested editor is open; keyboard focus on the rim/tools also reveals them. Hover reveal uses CSS without pointer-move matching or recipe/history writes, and registered controls remain mounted. Free/Realistic, ⠒ Atomnic, name/save, File and reset are adjacent rim tools, with pen/eraser last so toggling Atomnic does not shift preceding tools. Presets opens on right-click of empty editing space, not on the rim; it contains existing construction presets, workspace presets and saved operation tools. Hovering a category opens its child dial outside the parent dial along the hovered node’s radial axis (⚬-○), leaving the parent’s other contents unobscured. Leaving the child hides it; deeper levels repeat this placement. The Composer canvas stays in place; portals escape frame clipping. Dial centres stay exactly at the invocation point. Atomnic off/on preserves the same recipe and geometry. Ctrl/Command-left-drag displays a four-sided marquee and adds every rendered component intersecting its rectangular area, retaining existing picks. The shared content gesture boundary prevents the interface selector from stealing this drag unless interface-selection mode is explicitly enabled. The Composer closes its popup without consuming the selection press. MS priority remains intact. Direct left-drag moves existing targets; right-click during movement settles it and opens position settings. Wheel over the interior zooms the view (40–1000 extent), preserving browser Ctrl+wheel. Save/copy/import/export, live world drafts, history, recovery and library owners remain shared. Retired Object/Structure/Selection/Transform/Fill-marking/Motion/Inspection wrappers, Configure selected component, Operation scope and View zoom buttons remain absent. Color is a rainbow wheel, Fill ◐ and Opacity a faded ⬤. The last-position pen/eraser button uses the supplied eraser silhouette with upper white/lower black when offering Erase, reversed for Pen. Active cursors now inherit the activated tool icon through the website-wide shared cursor system. The purple hardcoded eraser cursor is removed. Button and cursor share the same two-tone no-underline silhouette; the button offers the next action while the cursor represents the active action. Tool cursor inheritance is now limited to the currently applicable operation zone. Leaving the editing circle for the tool rim or settings restores the normal cursor; returning restores the retained tool. Direct grabs show Move while held, then restore the retained operation. Edited-world image hit tests supply the same boundary rule. Empty-space right-click opens the preset radial. Choosing a preset shows all its currently applicable DOFs together around one circle. Numeric setter spokes appear while pressing/dragging their DOF icons, extending outward with the same length as the owning button diameter. Numeric strips use the shared slider; categorical strips cycle choices, toggles switch on/off, and color strips open the shared color editor. DOF right-click opens shared snap/step configuration. Choosing a preset commits it immediately to the draft. Accepted property changes persist independently; Enter/✓ only finishes editing. Esc/back or empty-space dismissal closes the dial without removing the chosen preset. Contextual dials at every category depth now pack icons around the centre button, using only the space required for the centre, neighbouring icons and any value strips. Fixed oversized dial radii are removed. All popup dials now inherit one radialLayout/RADIAL_GEOMETRY policy: equal centre/button size, count-based nonoverlap and a shared depth progression. Setters do not inflate the button radius. Viewport width no longer squeezes fixed-size slots together; large or edge-opened dials may clip. Automatic More tools overflow is removed everywhere; only explicit categories nest. Appearance DOFs (Color, Opacity and opacity progression) inherit one Appearance category from their shared input metadata in both target and preset dials. The existing mfx effects category lives beneath Appearance. Units/fill controls (Fill, Count, Size, Length, Stroke width and Stroke progression) inherit the ●● category; Radius and spatial controls (Rotation, Spacing, Gap progression, Centre offset and authored coordinates where applicable) share ⨮ Relations. This replaces the former ⟊ Position category rather than adding a separate category. Shared input metadata applies the same grouping to preset, target and MC dials. Standalone category dials show immediate child rows automatically; leaving them does not hide those rows. Embedded rim/deeper category navigation retains its existing reveal behavior. Drag a popup dial by its centre circle to reveal the underlying edits. A shared centre slider scales all popup dials from 1× to 2×, including buttons, spacing and spoke setters; the resident canvas size is unchanged. Scale is transient UI presentation and does not edit geometry/history. A category-centre click still goes Back; dragging does not. The origin handle has an interactive button role so shared empty-space dismissal never consumes its drag press. Position is transient and resets on a new invocation/stage. Movement uses only pointer capture and local translation, without scene edits or per-motion geometry queries. Popup buttons pack against their centre without reserving interior space for setters; equisized setter strips extend outward from their owner as radial spokes. Dragging follows the displayed axis, captured only at gesture start. Color has no value strip. Both target and preset DOF sliders are hidden at rest. Press and drag a numeric DOF icon: its spoke slider appears and the same gesture adjusts from the current value without jumping. Release commits and hides the slider; cancellation restores the previous value. Right-click keeps the existing snap/configuration path. Non-numeric tools retain their existing actions. The shared centre size slider remains visible only on the highest popup parent; child dials inherit its scale. Saved Omnic node visuals fit and centre the net composition using evaluated geometry bounds, independently of the Composer viewport position and zoom. Authored relative geometry and saved editor viewport remain intact. Temporary unsaved previews retain the editing viewport. Saved Omnic placements retain ordinary Atlas selection and dragging while the Composer is open; their live visuals update from Composer edits, but world gestures no longer invoke the Composer on saved nodes. Only the temporary unsaved preview borrows world editing. Live Omnic preview swaps retain node picking visibility and restore the original picking mesh visibility on dismissal. Child centres are empty draggable Back controls, with names in tooltips only. Opening guards track physical presses independently of UI ownership in the shared active-layer adapter, covering all registered popups rather than one dial component. Contextual popup stages consume the trailing pointer release and click of the press that opened them; a fresh press or keyboard activation works normally. Preset and target DOFs share registry property identities, editableDegrees discovery, target setters and common editors rather than preset-specific adjustment handlers. Child spacing uses the parent and child visible button footprints plus a 2px gap, excluding hidden setter margins and accounting for dial scale. Child category centres retain their computed outward anchor instead of being reanchored to the cursor by nested editor stages. Category children open on hover and remain open inside the visible child rim circle, including gaps between controls; the outer slider/layout margin is excluded; they collapse after leaving the category and its child zone. Size uses ●⬤ and Radius uses ⊖. The ◎ Nested rings preset inserts a count-controlled ring generator (1–64). Its shared DOFs set innermost radius, radial gap, gap progression, centre drift per ring and direction, fill, stroke width/progression, color, opacity/progression. Defaults are concentric, equally spaced and unfilled. Existing authored ring groups remain editable. Generated ring roles have stable index identities; changing count preserves surviving indices. Generated roles do not yet have individual persistent overrides; use authored rings for independent edits. Invalid extent/work-budget results are rejected. Member and Part / half-unit concept presets are removed from the preset list; existing saved constructions remain intact. All construction and saved presets occupy direct slots around the preset dial; adding presets grows that ring instead of creating an additional-tools submenu. Position X/Y use distinct ⊕X / ⊕Y icons and appear under Relations for every target/preset declaring writable coordinates, including lines and nested rings. Dragging and sliders edit the same stored properties through shared discovery and target setters; direct manipulation does not hide a property from editors. Left-clicking empty space dismisses all open contextual dials and requested dial editors, consuming that press so it does not also draw or begin a world gesture. Dial ×/close buttons are removed; the middle circle remains an unlabelled origin marker at full opacity. Category Back and Escape still step outward. Controls and rendered target roles retain their own click handling. Empty-space dismissal preserves chosen presets and accepted settings. Line and Ring are standalone presets; Ring no longer inserts an array. Oscillation is removed from construction presets and appears as the sole current motion effect under the rim category labelled/iconed mfx. Effects are discovered from operator metadata. Applying mfx → Oscillation uses selected geometry (the whole composition when no selection exists), adds no new geometry and opens the same radial DOF settings. Reopening the same target effect retains its operation identity/settings. The existing bounded animation preview is started when allowed. Dial centres anchor exactly at their opening click. Radial shells no longer carry the rectangular popup surface class. Authored geometry declares its fill and stroke directly as SVG styles. Rim circles explicitly have no fill; empty popup area passes canvas input through. Authored structural SVG colors opt out of browser automatic dark recoloring. Entire popup dials default to 100% opacity, including tools and setters; drag the centre circle to see underlying edits. New constructions and workspace presets now insert alongside previous contents at the empty-space click. Internal component/operation/frame identities and scopes are remapped; external object references retain canonical identity. Only the inserted structure becomes selected. MC Active context uses existing Delete, F focus, M edge-fit/restore, W edge-fit/restore, D numeric expansion/compression and Compact commands through a shared target adapter. Multiple compatible DOFs open one shared radial choice before execution; one compatible DOF runs directly. Selected geometry lends existing properties to MC through the common property bindings. Close is not geometry deletion and is unavailable there. Category children now form a shared compact row of 24px controls with 2px gaps along the parent’s outward radial axis. Authored atoms retain Micro/Macro and Free/Realistic legality: Free decouples imprint/step; Realistic uses the touching triangular lattice and rejects illegal placements without changing geometry. Normal components translate through registered position adapters. Right-click during movement settles the move and opens progressive scope → constraints → step settings for the next drag. Stationary target right-click discovers other common writable DOFs in one flat ring, without file/category actions or Procedural X/Y/Move buttons. R/Rotation opens the shared value slider; its explicit mode starts at ✣ Symmetry · 2³. The separate Step action retains the old pivot workflow. Scale is transient UI presentation and does not edit geometry/history. A category-centre click still goes Back; dragging does not. Dragging follows the displayed axis, captured only at gesture start. Color has no value strip. Both target and preset DOF sliders are hidden at rest. Press and drag a numeric DOF icon: its spoke slider appears and the same gesture adjusts from the current value without jumping. Release commits and hides the slider; cancellation restores the previous value. Right-click keeps the existing snap/configuration path. Non-numeric tools retain their existing actions. The shared centre size slider remains visible only on the highest popup parent; child dials inherit its scale. All construction and saved presets occupy direct slots around the preset dial; adding presets grows that ring instead of creating an additional-tools submenu. Dragging and sliders edit the same stored properties through shared discovery and target setters; direct manipulation does not hide a property from editors. Left-clicking empty space dismisses all open contextual dials and requested dial editors, consuming that press so it does not also draw or begin a world gesture. Dial ×/close buttons are removed; the middle circle remains an unlabelled origin marker at full opacity. Category Back and Escape still step outward. Controls and rendered target roles retain their own click handling. Empty-space dismissal preserves chosen presets and accepted settings. Opening/collapsing a frame preserves appearance target metadata when ownership and captions are unchanged. Appearance adjusters reuse target calculations; hidden dock areas skip measurement. Hot function controls now subscribe to their own item, binding, selection and permission slices instead of the full UI context. Stable appearance context actions keep current handlers without broadcasting closure changes. Legacy consumers retain their existing route during incremental migration. Fields, action registrations and embedded headers use scoped subscriptions. Dock workspace geometry/context preserve identity when unchanged; appearance label invalidation follows actual customized owners, not unrelated frame registration order. Floating windows, panels, frame chrome, docking residents and labels now use scoped subscriptions. Closed frame searches and dormant popup adapters do not subscribe to unrelated UI updates. Native caption/button discovery deduplicates inserted subtrees and updates changed hosts directly; unchanged native presentation skips DOM writes and permission work. Discovered function registrations publish once per microtask while commands/history remain synchronous. With no UI controls selected, ordinary layout changes now skip UI-selection discovery and visibility measurement. Subscription snapshot checks reuse pure selector results for the same committed snapshot and selector; changed state or captured props still reevaluate. Window movement now coalesces pointer positions per frame, reuses target lists and caches ownership/pinning/context/docking reads until the layout snapshot changes. Final release refreshes the pointed destination and uses the existing single-commit history path. Newly discovered frame captions now read their initial font sizes together before symbol/tooltip styling writes. This avoids repeated synchronous style recalculation during first-use presentation; later collapse/reopen keeps existing caption state. Drag pickup excludes a frame/window’s own subtree from destination measurements, snapshots visibility before lifting, and uses an exact resident lookup. Final destination refresh and shared docking/history remain intact. Repeated activation of the current front window reuses its existing layer rather than changing z-index and rerendering the wrapper on each grab; other windows still rise. Fixed surfaces already mounted directly on the page move using their existing transform without popover promotion or geometry rewrites. Drag destination bounds are cached on demand; child-slot measurement is limited to destinations actually considered. Cursor-open windows use viewport free placement on both rendering and drop, avoiding workspace packing on release. Drag capture no longer toggles a descendant CSS selector across the whole page. Release deduplicates pointed ancestor measurements, reuses gesture candidate lists. Final placement continues to use the exact release coordinate; no inertia is implemented. Moving an already-free frame validates its new coordinates and preserves unrelated layout records instead of rerunning structural detach/prune/full validation. The held payload now receives a direct transform update from each pointer event; docking discovery/feedback alone stays frame-batched. Movement does not wait for docking calculations or interpolate toward the cursor. Release now hands direct visual ownership back to committed layout synchronously, preventing a paint of the pre-drag position between them. The interface state owner recognizes immutable coordinate-only edits and validates the changed coordinates without rechecking unchanged topology; other edits/imports retain full validation.

Leaving all applicable zones restores the native cursor, including selection/hand/text/resize behavior over controls. Omnic registers its circular editing surface with cached geometry; the world adapter publishes its existing edited-image hit test without another raycast. Pointer capture cannot extend a tool beyond its visible zone. Direct grabs temporarily select the Move cursor and restore the retained tool on release. MS explicitly applies page-wide outside selector/settings chrome, preserving live precision, priority and parking; parked MS keeps its marker and restores native pointing. The clicked icon/custom appearance is captured once, before a toggle offers its next action; keyboard/default activation uses the same declared icon. Pointer movement updates only the current transform and cached zone checks; React updates only at operation/zone transitions. Style capture is activation-only, bounded to 128 icon nodes. Pen and Erase share a no-underline silhouette: Pen upper black/lower white; Erase upper white/lower black. The button offers the next action while the cursor shows the active applicable operation. The last alignment/performance changes were reverted at user request. Default tool icons are simply centred on the actual pointer, with no snapped-marker tracking or preview subscription. MS keeps its explicit precision anchor. ToolIcon metadata can declare a glyph size and glow once; shared ToolGlyph applies them to both tool controls and default cursors. Rotation uses a 20px glowing glyph. Captured clicked-icon appearance retains that glyph styling.

steps.do: Activate Erase, move into the Composer editing interior, then move onto the circular rim and tool buttons. Return to the editing interior.
steps.expect: Erase uses upper white/lower black inside its valid area. Leaving the editing circle restores the normal browser cursor; selecting tools no longer carries an eraser cursor. Returning restores the retained Erase operation.

steps.do: Repeat inside an edited Omnium image, then move onto another world node or empty world background.
steps.expect: The tool cursor applies only over the edited image. Other world regions keep normal navigation cursors; no extra raycast is added for cursor selection.

steps.do: Activate MS, enter its controls, park/resume it, then close it and disable Atomnic.
steps.expect: MS has priority only where its operation applies; its controls retain normal interaction. Parking preserves the marker/native pointer. Closing it restores whichever underlying tool applies at the pointer; disabling Atomnic restores native pointing when no tool applies.

steps.do: Customize a tool icon through existing appearance controls and activate it by clicking its icon.
steps.expect: Within its valid zone the cursor uses that clicked appearance. Leaving the zone restores native pointing; later appearance edits refresh on the next activation.

steps.do: Move Pen and Erase inside the canvas, then leave for the tools.
steps.expect: The icon centre is on the actual cursor position; it follows the pointer directly. There is no marker-following mechanism. Zone-based native-cursor restoration remains.

entries.status: Shared cursor system implemented; interaction acceptance pending
entries.limits: Features declare their unique active state and zone, then inherit resolution, icon capture and transport. DOM zones cache bounds on entry/resize/scroll; non-DOM adapters publish their existing hit-test result. Only explicitly page-wide tools declare zone "*". Custom appearance snapshots are activation-only (up to 128 icon nodes); keyboard/default activation falls back to the declared icon if no snapshot exists. entries.title: MC commands inherit the active geometry target
entries.where: Click geometry in the Omnic radar or its edited world image, then MC → Active context; retained shortcuts Delete, F, M, W and D use the same commands.
entries.behavior: Shared target adapters resolve supported operations from the selected members to enclosing groups and the composition. Existing command IDs, shortcut configuration, MC projection, property pool and draft/history owners are reused. Delete removes selected construction while preserving unrelated identities, repairs explicit operation/frame scopes without turning an emptied scope into all, and is undoable. F fits the construction view to the active scope. M fits a compatible length DOF to nearest sibling/parent/view edges and restores its previous value on repeat; W uses the same edge-fit/restore operation. D doubles a selected numeric DOF (or compresses when already at its bound), then restores its prior value on repeat. M/W/D ask which DOF when several qualify; this disambiguation is global in the target-command runtime, not Composer-specific. One qualifying DOF executes directly. Compact reuses shared packing on selected authored components/group members. MC edits common/declared group-member properties through existing setters. Close does not apply to geometry; clicking the parent frame restores existing frame actions. MS keeps first shortcut priority; active held gestures retain Escape cancellation. Shift uses the existing configuration router: cycles/hover select a DOF, release applies, right-click applies/locks its priority, left-click resets priority 1. Normal multi-DOF invocation still asks.

steps.do: Select a normal line/ring or several Atomnic members. Open MC → Active context.
steps.expect: MC names the geometry scope and projects supported existing controls, including Delete selection. Geometry properties come from registered inputs. No second Composer frame toolbar is added; Close is unavailable for geometry.

steps.do: Press D or click Expand/compress. Choose a numeric DOF from the radial, then repeat the operation on the same DOF.
steps.expect: When several DOFs qualify, nothing changes before the choice. Choosing performs bounded numeric inflation; repeating restores the previous value. A single compatible DOF runs directly. Changing selection before choosing prevents the stale operation from affecting a replacement target.

steps.do: Use M and select a size/radius/thickness/spacing DOF where available. Repeat to restore, then W to use the same edge-fit/restore operation.
steps.expect: M uses nearest surrounding edges and validated numeric bounds. W uses the same supported edge-fit operation. Exact values remain editable through MC properties or target DOF controls. Geometry constraints may reject an illegal edit without altering the construction.

steps.do: Hold Shift and press D or M; cycle or hover choices, release Shift. Right-click a choice in configuration, then reopen configuration and left-click to reset.
steps.expect: The existing shared gesture applies once; right-click retains its priority in the shared function-value settings, and left-click restores priority 1. Normal invocation continues to ask when ambiguous.

steps.do: Select multiple components or a group and use Compact; then Delete selection and Undo. Press Esc through selection/group/composition contexts; click frame chrome and use its existing commands.
steps.expect: Supported targets compact through the shared packing helper. Delete changes construction, not window visibility; Undo restores it. Esc steps through narrower contexts first. Frame commands retain their original behavior once frame chrome is active.

entries.status: Implemented for review in the open PR; not merged to production
entries.limits: This integrates MC with authored Omnic geometry, not the full MS clipping/selection engine. Expansion currently uses a bounded factor-two toggle; exact value/step/halving adjustments remain in the shared property editor. M uses evaluated rectangular sibling/parent/view edges and consumer numeric bounds; the circular viewport may clip corners. Parameter/property permissions and Realistic lattice constraints remain authoritative. Compact is limited to 32 authored targets, rejects illegal Realistic results and does not unpack generated array units into new identities. Shift priority retains the existing ordinal 1–10 domain. View-fit extent retains 40–1000. Target adapters for other systems opt into this common mechanism by declaring their actual capabilities. Edge fit is limited to 256 evaluated roles and uses a bounded three-snapshot linear solution with final verification; nonlinear/identity-changing transforms reject without a partial edit.

verification.browser: Pending user interaction acceptance; no browser suite run.
verification.automated: Models cover nearest scope, zero/one/many DOFs, stale choice cancellation, source cleanup, MS and gesture shortcut precedence, nested deletion scopes, independent insertion and shared packing. Type/property/backend/preview checks run before publication.

entries.title: Child controls open at the invoking cursor point
entries.where: Shared contextual MC, DOF/property stages, numeric/halving editors, context submenus and frame/global search.
entries.behavior: The shared popup anchor captures the invocation position. A radial centres on it; a rectangular child starts there. Shared PropertyEditor and ProgressiveConfiguration announce only logical field/page changes, so successive setters open at the new click. Same-title custom stages may declare a stable stage key. Context menus, submenus and search use the existing shared cursor source. Ordinary value/hover updates do not reposition an open popup, and a held slider gesture cannot trigger reanchoring when conditional controls appear. No pointer polling, new pointer listeners or broad DOM scans are introduced. Viewport fitting does not displace an opening popup from its invocation point.

steps.do: Open a preset DOF radial, click a DOF, then move the cursor and advance a configuration step.
steps.expect: The child field appears at its own invoking click; the next page uses its invoking click too. Parent/tool identity and retained values stay intact.

steps.do: Open a numeric value/limit/jump editor and halving picker, a context submenu, and frame/global search from different pointer positions.
steps.expect: Shared child popups start at the invoking cursor point across these systems. Moving the pointer or changing a value does not make the existing popup follow it.

steps.do: Drag a slider that reveals a conditional control, then release. Open a popup near a viewport edge.
steps.expect: The held gesture keeps its original geometry; the popup does not jump during dragging. Edge invocation preserves the origin and may clip content; reopening farther inside restores access.

entries.status: Implemented for review in the open PR; not merged to production

entries.title: ⠒❉ shared raw-number dial (Composer)
entries.where: Composer numeric DOF → click its mode expression, rule variable or slider end-limit control. Search ⠒❉ or mathematical dial.
entries.behavior: ⠒❉ makes/configures the rule and its numeric variables. It does not traverse the object value. The shared value slider performs execution. Existing signed numeral brushes, accumulated marks, recursion, ring growth and exact fractional parameter entry remain available for rule configuration. Clicking a selected slot removes its mark. A hold gesture chooses fill or erase from its starting slot and applies that intent consistently across visited slots; repeated crossings never toggle marks back. Hover and keyboard activation preview/use the same operation. Property limits still reject illegal totals. Hover/focus leaves committed slot fills unchanged and indicates the candidate with rim glow only. Held fill/erase gestures still display their stroke preview. The entire mathematical dial is now 1.5× its previous displayed size (CSS zoom 0.75 instead of 0.5), including slots and meta controls; slot capacity and numeric rules are unchanged.

steps.do: Open a numeric DOF, click its mode expression and change the mathematical number.
steps.expect: The generated values change without modifying the actual object value.

steps.do: Right-click the math ring to cycle its numeral brush, then select/paint marks.
steps.expect: Marks configure the rule parameter. The value slider remains the place to execute generated values.

steps.do: Right-click a slider end bar and use the math dial readout for an exact fractional limit where the domain permits it.
steps.expect: Exact fractional rule/limit values remain supported; the actual DOF is not edited until a slider value is executed.

steps.do: Select several slots, then click one selected slot again. Hold from a selected slot and sweep across others.
steps.expect: The clicked slot deselects. The held sweep erases crossed selected slots without toggling them back on; starting on an empty slot still fills. Invalid totals remain constrained by the property domain.

steps.do: Hover a selected slot, then an empty one; compare the dial size and perform a held fill/erase sweep.
steps.expect: Selected fills stay visible under hover; empty slots stay unfilled and only their rim glows. The complete dial is 1.5× larger. Held stroke previews and click deselection still work.

entries.limits: Composer-only refinement. Slot notation is signed whole numbers; decimal notation, additional rule families/equations, relational constraints and candidate/action ranking are deferred. Native exact entry preserves existing fractional editing. Count-grid domain0–512; each other consumer retains its real limits and Realistic legality. Base1 recursion unsupported; four ring orders maximum. Marks/brush remain session-local; reopening shows the stored raw value with a fresh scratch numeral. Undo restores properties, not the complete expression. Color spectrum gestures, dial-size controls and outside-Composer snap configuration retain their working specialized controls. Browser acceptance pending.

entries.title: Reference selection with the Q selector
entries.where: Composer active DOF → top ⟴ button → the existing Q selector → click an object inside Composer.
entries.behavior: The ⟴ button invokes the same selector.open action as Q, using its existing controls, configuration and pointer selection. No intermediate reference dial, custom list or forced Master Controller window is opened. Composer exposes declared selectable geometry and stable identities scoped to its editing surface. Picking a compatible object sets the active DOF reference without changing geometry; picking the active object restores Self, and picking the empty Composer surface uses Environment where supported. Acceptance checks canonical reference compatibility and the current Composer surface. The previous selector selection/configuration are restored on acceptance or cancellation. Ordinary Q selection also selects the corresponding authored Composer object.

steps.do: Press Q over Composer and use its existing selector to click an object.
steps.expect: The object is selected in Composer through the same selector; selection identity survives Composer SVG feedback refreshes.

steps.do: Activate a numeric DOF and click top ⟴; use the Q selector to click another object inside Composer.
steps.expect: The existing Q controls open directly, with no list or intermediate reference dial. Compatible geometry becomes the reference without changing the edited geometry.

steps.expect: Self or Environment is selected spatially; no separate options list is needed.

steps.do: Open reference selection, then press Esc.
steps.expect: The previous reference, geometry and selector selection/configuration are retained.

Arbitrary 3D-canvas feature picking and persistent relationship solvers remain deferred. Active rotation/oscillation scenes remain conservatively unavailable for authored reference measurements. Unsupported choices keep the selector active.

entries.title: Rule-configured values and rotation axis wheel
entries.where: Composer → right-click an authored object → choose a DOF. Rotation opens the axis wheel; R on a compatible selection also opens it. Geometry-based hover/edge activation is temporarily disabled.
entries.behavior:
Composer numeric DOFs share generated rule/constraint fields, existing property setters/history and preview/commit sessions. The active top strip exposes DOF, mode/expression and ⟴ reference with tooltips; it is absent without an active DOF. Right-click an object to choose its DOF. Geometry-based hover tool detection and precision edge-click activation are temporarily disabled by HOVER_TOOL_DETECTION_ENABLED, with the implementation retained for future review. Ordinary object dragging and explicit tools remain available.

Rotation and other declared cyclic DOFs use the shared axis wheel; R on a compatible selection opens the same editor. Hover a wheel direction to preview, primary release commits and stays open, leaving restores an uncommitted preview, Enter confirms, and clicking outside dismisses. The centre is neutral/drag-only. Bare rays show generated states; significant axes use stronger strokes. Noncyclic DOFs use shared RangeControl value execution: drag previews, release commits, arrows/wheel/keyboard traverse generated values. MathematicalDial configures rule variables. Limit editors select from thresholds/fractions, reachable from the slider ends or mode ⊢/⊣. No companion execution slider appears during configuration/reference picking.

⟴ opens common reference options; the source control there explicitly invokes Q/MS. MS configuration Enter resumes aiming like ✓; pending aiming reference Enter confirms its candidate, with selector priority over underlying popup/native button activation. Self, compatible authored objects and supported environment boundaries supply reference context. Bounds use of coordinate references provides default intervals and centre/boundary thresholds; working limits override defaults under hard owner limits. Changing reference resets bounds while retaining the rule. Valid declared domain/reference thresholds survive mathematical rule changes, with stable identity/provenance and owner-legality filtering. Cyclic domains inherit quarter-turn axes; opacity declares transparent/opaque states. Old numeric preset arrays are not promoted to semantic thresholds. Reference/limit configuration preserves geometry; execution applies through existing owners. Retained single-target Position dragging uses the same field generation and limit resolution.

Standalone DOF category dials display immediate child rows on opening, without hover. Rows stay open until their parent closes and align to measured parent-button centres/edges. Embedded rim/deeper category reveal behavior remains. Shared popup placement, scale, appearance, right-click sub-setters and outside-dismissal ownership are retained. Button-triggered editors remain below their invoking controls; contextual stage changes do not add cursor-following information. Reference use is now explicit: open ⟴ options to choose Bounds, Step or Match and a compatible source measurement. Step does not import source bounds; Match offers the exact result. ×/÷ use the existing mathematical dial to configure measured ratios. See Reference measurements as bounds, step or match for the complete flow. Position now uses this same editor, preserving Partitions/fractions, with joint Match and optional component settings; the separate Centre-action dial is removed. The rule expression displays a count of one as 1, not 2⁰; larger exact powers retain compact power notation.

steps.do: Open Composer with no active DOF, then activate one by editing an object. Hover and click its top icons.
steps.expect: No strip is shown while inactive. Activation shows an icon-only strip inside the circle; tooltips identify its DOF, mode, rule variables and reference, and clicking opens the corresponding editor.

steps.do: Open Count, Size or Opacity. Drag the value slider and release; repeat and cancel with Esc.
steps.expect: Dragging previews prepared values, release commits once, and Esc restores the original value. The same slider handles every numeric DOF without a bespoke value dial.

steps.do: Click the top Mode control (right-click chooses a mode), choose Halving, close settings, then drag or scroll the value slider.
steps.expect: It visits the actual generated sequence (for example 1.25, 2.5, 5, 10), without inventing interpolated values. Halving is a rule, not a replacement slider or a separate ½ picker.

steps.do: Right-click the left end bar and edit the minimum; right-click the right bar and edit the maximum.
steps.expect: Limits are attached to the slider ends. Configuring them filters the available sequence without changing geometry. Reset ↺ in a bound editor restores working limits. Empty sequences disable execution while leaving the limit controls editable.

steps.do: Click the rule expression (such as 2³) at the top, edit its number, then return to the slider.
steps.expect: The math dial modifies the rule; the slider updates to traverse its output. The object value changes only when the value slider executes a choice.

steps.do: Use the slider arrows, wheel and keyboard arrows. Right-click its track to type an exact generated value.
steps.expect: All execution paths select members of the same prepared sequence. Typed values outside the sequence are rejected with a prompt to change the rule; native non-rule sliders retain their existing numeric-entry behavior.

steps.do: Drag one authored object; click the top ⟴ reference → the Q selector. Click another compatible object, the edited object for Self, or the empty Composer surface for Environment, then traverse the slider. MB3 alternatively toggles the settings radial.
steps.expect: the top information remains clickable after release. Q reference selection preserves appearance targeting and MS selection on accept/cancel. Reference/limits use canonical evaluated geometry including parent offsets; configuration itself preserves geometry.

steps.do: Open settings from the top strip or value slider, then open a nested rule/bound editor.
steps.expect: The child remains separate from the invoking strip and every open contextual ancestor. Changing settings does not stack transparent controls over the same position.

steps.do: Drag an object, then click the top reference icon, mode or expression; repeat through a nested button.
steps.expect: No DOF-information echo follows the cursor. The requested editor opens below its invoking button, without an extra position slider beside configuration. Returning from settings/Q reference selection restores the value slider.

steps.do: While moving an object or dragging a noncyclic value slider, right-click; for Rotation, right-click the open wheel.
steps.expect: Shared DOF settings open and can be dismissed outside their zone. Rotation itself is chosen by hovering/clicking the wheel, not by dragging the object.

steps.do: Open the wheel and release the opening click. Hover a direction, leave the wheel, then hover/click another direction and leave again.
steps.expect: Opening does not commit an angle. Leaving an uncommitted preview restores the original angle; leaving after clicking preserves the committed angle. Esc cancels preview and outside clicks dismiss.

steps.do: Open Position X/Y on one authored object. Click ⟴ and select Self, another compatible object or the empty environment.
steps.expect: Q returns to the value editor with the selected source’s default interval and centre/boundary states. Picking Self retains it as a source. Reference configuration leaves geometry unchanged.

steps.do: Right-click a slider end bar, or open the Mode configuration and choose ⊢/⊣. Traverse the limit slider, release to retain that bound, then press Enter to return to execution.
steps.expect: Bound choices come from the current reference’s generated fractions and significant thresholds. Geometry stays unchanged until an execution value is applied. Reset restores reference defaults; switching source clears old bound overrides.

steps.do: Change Rotation divisions to 7 or 31, then hover near North/East/South/West. Change numeric fractional rules with a declared significant threshold.
steps.expect: Valid significant states remain exact selectable candidates across rules, with stronger rotation axis rays. Hard constraints and owner legality can exclude a threshold.

steps.do: Open ⟴ options, choose its source control, press Enter instead of ✓ in MS configuration, then select a reference. Repeat using ✓.
steps.expect: Both enter the same aiming flow; Enter does not activate the focused reference button or open a resize dial. Native input Enter and polygon completion remain unchanged.

steps.do: Right-click a target, choose Rotation, or select a compatible target and press R. Hover/click a direction in its wheel.
steps.expect: Explicit DOF selection opens the existing preview/commit wheel. Merely hovering object edges has no tool-detection or rotation activation effect.

steps.do: Set Divisions to 1 using the first base-1 slot.
steps.expect: The top expression reads 1. Counts such as 8 still read 2³; the value itself is unchanged.

entries.limits: Composer rule execution currently supports finite numeric fields with bounds, integrality and existing owner legality. Values are sorted for the ordinary left-to-right value slider; its limit bars show constraints, which need not themselves be generated values. Up to 64 divisions plus endpoints/reference landmarks, or eight halving samples. General geometry solvers, symbolic equations, nonnumeric field adapters and persistent constraints remain pending. Active transformed/animated scenes remain conservatively unavailable for authored-reference matching. Gesture rule retention and boundary references currently cover single authored targets and individual coordinate axes; boundary landmarks do not enforce containment. Reference picking resolves compatible canonical authored Composer objects; arbitrary pixel/3D features remain deferred. Multi-target dragging retains its previous behavior. Below-button editors do not automatically flip above their button at viewport edges. The local Composer uses the SVG-to-CSS-pixel scale exactly; the existing world-preview bridge supplies a local projected-plane pixel metric. Supported rendered primitives are line capsules and filled/stroked circles. Measurement-feature/use selection is implemented in the reference-use radial; persistent geometry bindings remain pending. Self position intervals derive from committed evaluated bounds; repeated commits can refresh that context. Arbitrary per-DOF semantic thresholds still require adapter declarations; an empty declaration does not invent meaning.

Unselected-hover regression verifies move/rotation capability discovery, absence of unsupported actions, and preservation of source recipe/selection; existing geometry/ref ownership tests cover shared authored-node resolution. Axis-wheel regressions cover neutral centre/opening, North/right/South directions, hover restoration, captured click commitment after focus cancellation and preservation of committed values. Existing shared relative-slider scrub tests remain for DOF-icon drags, not rotation-edge execution. New model tests verify Self/external interval resolution, overridable defaults under hard bounds, threshold preservation across rules/divisions, owner legality and future cyclic-domain inheritance.

entries.title: Reference measurements as bounds, step or match
entries.where: Omnic Composer → numeric DOF → ⟴ reference options. Choose the source control inside those options for Q/MS; choose measurement and Bounds/Step/Match in the same shared configuration.
entries.behavior: Source selection and measurement use are independent. The source is retained per authored target across DOF changes. Opening ⟴ options does not automatically invoke selection; only its source control does. Per-target/per-DOF relation settings choose a compatible measurement and Bounds (⊢⊣), Step (Δ) or Match (⨮). The top ⟴ control shows a small use glyph and descriptive tooltip. Spatial reference context supplies its existing boundary defaults; explicit measured extents can instead supply a zero-to-measure interval. Step uses the measured magnitude without inheriting source position bounds. Match offers exactly the measured result, independent of the previous generated sequence. Configuration preserves geometry; existing slider/wheel preview and explicit commitment apply values through normal property setters/history. The shared source adapter reads canonical evaluated bounds (width/height), declared radius/length and compatible numeric DOFs. Self and Environment use the same path where supported. Geometry measurement ratios are configured with × multiplier and ÷ divisor through the existing math dial; display readouts are compact but calculations retain precision. Coordinate match ratios apply before converting from scene measurements to authored coordinates. Units, integrality, hard bounds, explicit working limits and owner legality remain authoritative. Selecting a different source retains the measurement/use choice; if that feature is unavailable, execution is disabled until the user selects a supported feature. Several DOFs may use the same source feature for different purposes; their editing contexts refresh when that committed source changes. Existing direct single-target Position dragging consumes the same resolved field as its slider. Sharing source identity does not silently activate constraints on other DOFs: direct Position prepares only explicitly configured axes or retained axis rules. Picking a source, configuring a use or committing its field activates that consumer; its unconfigured companion axis stays free.

steps.do: Create two lines. Open Position → ⊕X on the first, open ⟴ options, choose its source control, press Enter or ✓ to aim MS, then pick the second line.
steps.expect: The source is retained; Bounds is the explicit default use. Selection itself does not move the line.

steps.do: Open ⟴ options. Choose Δ Step, click the ↔ Measurement control, then choose Length (↗). Press Enter to return to execution. Drag the Position slider or the object.
steps.expect: Movement visits steps equal to the source line’s length, anchored to the edited position. It is not constrained to the source’s positional boundary. Direct single-target movement and slider execution use the same sequence.

steps.do: Reopen reference-use configuration and set ÷ to 2 with the mathematical dial. Return to execution.
steps.expect: The step is half the selected source length. × sets a numerator; ÷ sets the divisor. Ordinary rule controls route to this measured-use configuration while a step/match relation is active, rather than showing an ignored generator.

steps.do: Open Length on the first line. The reference source remains selected. Open ⟴ options, select Length as the measurement and ⨮ Match as its use. Close configuration and click the value slider.
steps.expect: The exact source length is previewed/committed through the existing owner. Position’s Step relation is retained independently and both consumer contexts derive from the same source identity.

steps.do: Change the source line’s length and reopen the consumers. Pick Self as source and repeat with Width/Height.
steps.expect: Editing contexts resolve the updated measurement. Self is a measured source too. Previously committed dependent geometry is not automatically rewritten; persistent geometry binding is not implemented.

steps.do: Choose ⊢⊣ Bounds and the Boundary/compatible extent measurement, then refine slider-end limits.
steps.expect: Only Bounds use applies source interval defaults. Step and Match retain hard/explicit consumer constraints without importing the source interval. Unsupported units/features/zero steps or illegal matches produce no executable value.

entries.limits: Composer-only experimental editing context, transient to the open Composer session. Single authored targets and the existing untransformed evaluated geometry adapters are supported; enabled rotation/oscillation scenes remain conservatively unavailable for reference use. Direct Position fields remain individual X/Y axes, not a general spatial solver. Measurement selection is per consumer DOF; source identity is shared across its DOFs. Compatible unit declarations are required for future adapters. No persistent dependent-geometry updates, dependency graph, cycle solver or saved binding mode yet.
